source.title: Latent Spaces Beyond Synthesis: From GANs to Diffusion Models

record.file_problem: none; the full text is present. Details of the layer-injection setup and results are referred to Schaerf et al. (2025), rather than fully reported here.
record.tranche_reason: The paper presents qualitative results from layerwise representation interventions and explicitly argues that diffusion models' differing internal arrangements challenge the Platonic Representation Hypothesis. It does not measure cross-model distance alignment or its change with scale.
record.gate_note: The text reports that injecting one image's layer representation into another image's generation reveals specialized layers and different placements of those layers across diffusion models. It gives no numerical results or detailed layer-by-layer intervention outcomes. Statements about density, smoothness, organization, and relevance of individual diffusion-model spaces do not compare independently trained models, so they are not recorded as rows. The claimed experiment is attributed to Schaerf et al. (2025); the current text gives a qualitative summary.
record.test_reason: The paper argues against the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, but its evidence is a qualitative layer-injection experiment on several diffusion models. It shows where structure, content and surface-detail roles sit in each model's layer stack. That is functional layer placement, not the similarity of representations of the same inputs across models, which is what V1 names. No alignment measure, scale sweep or cross-model mapping is reported. It measures a related but different construct, so it does not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors argue that diffusion models spread representation across specialized layers (a 'synthesis in a broad sense') rather than one latent space that determines the output. They contest the Platonic Representation Hypothesis because layer arrangements differ across models, while conceding that components may appear similar. The experiment's full results are deferred to Schaerf et al. (2025).
record.recipe_differences: The study uses layerwise representation injection to examine specialization and placement, rather than measuring similarity of representations across models as in the claim's original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The text reports model-dependent differences in which layers carry content, structure, and surface details; it does not report sensitivity to similarity metrics or their settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Across U-Net and transformer diffusion models (SD1.4, SD2, SDXL, Kandinsky, SD3.5, Flux), layer injection reveals layers specialized for structure, content and surface details. Where those layers sit differs by model, and the evidence is qualitative only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different generative models share a functional division of representational labour across layers, but place it at different depths. Under this view, similarity is of components, not of layer arrangement.

record.problems: The text gives no numerical outcomes, uncertainty estimates, control conditions, model sizes, or detailed layer indices. The intervention setup and full results are delegated to a cited paper, and the summary does not report cross-model distance alignment or scaling.

untested.parts: No representational similarity across models, no scale or capability trend.
All of it. Injection is within a single model, between two images.
All of it. Functional roles are not identified as shared features.

record.verdict_notes: This is a humanities/media-theory essay. The anti-PRH argument conflates where roles sit in the layer stack with whether representations of the same data converge; the experiment does not measure the latter. The finding that all models develop the same three-way specialization could even be read as weak functional convergence. The reader's V1 'challenges' label is removed.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep; no direct comparison of distances between the same inputs, and no measure of alignment across independently trained models. The reported comparison concerns qualitative layerwise organization in diffusion models.
No paired image-caption alignment comparison or performance sweep.
No comparison across random initializations or shared-subspace analysis.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment test between models.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, or circuits are identified across models.
No alternative similarity measures, parameter settings, or input distributions are compared.
The text does not test whether shared data or objectives explain alignment, nor quantify alignment plateaus or incompleteness.

rows.subject: almost all diffusion models considered
rows.operation_detail: Injected a representation from image E at a layer into the generation of image O, switching at each timestep.

conditions.value: layerwise representation from image E into image O generation

rows.measure: Qualitative specialization of layerwise representations into image structure, content, and surface details/colors; cross-model arrangement of these roles.
rows.value: The paper reports one or more layers responsible for image structure, one or more for content, and one or more for surface details and colors; their locations differ between models.
rows.note: Aggregate statement across the models considered. The paper says components may appear similar, but their internal arrangements differ. No cross-model distance or alignment score is given.
rows.check: This is an aggregate, qualitative statement about which layers play which role in each model. Layer placement of roles is not cross-model representational alignment, so it cannot show V1's effect. The text also says most models put content layers first; the row does not record this.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion 1.4
rows.operation_detail: Injected a representation from image E at a layer into the generation of image O, switching at each timestep.

conditions.value: layerwise representation from image E into image O generation

rows.measure: Relative placement of layers responsible for image content and surface details.
rows.value: Content layers occur after surface layers.
rows.note: A qualitative finding about the arrangement of specialized layers, not a direct similarity-distance measurement.
rows.check: SD1.4 places content layers after surface layers. This is the ordering of roles within one model, not an alignment measure.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion 2
rows.operation_detail: Injected a representation from image E at a layer into the generation of image O, switching at each timestep.

conditions.value: layerwise representation from image E into image O generation

rows.measure: Location of the most critical layers in the model.
rows.value: The most critical layers are in the late encoder.
rows.note: The paper groups Stable Diffusion 2 with Stable Diffusion 1.4 when describing late-encoder layers.
rows.check: SD2 has its critical layers in the late encoder (grouped with SD1.4 in the text). This is a within-model placement, not an alignment measure.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Qualitative comparisons of layerwise arrangements in the diffusion models described
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports specialized representational roles but different internal arrangements across models, and uses this to contest convergence; the evidence is qualitative and does not measure distance alignment or scale (r1-r7).
